question: Which metal lies between magnesium and iron in the activity series?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **activity series of metals**, also known as the reactivity series, is a list of metals arranged in the order of their reactivity from highest to lowest.
 
• **Magnesium** is a highly reactive metal, and it lies above many other metals in the activity series.
 
• **Zinc** lies between magnesium and iron in the activity series. It is less reactive than magnesium but more reactive than iron. *Hence, the correct answer is Zinc.*
 
• **Copper**, **silver**, and **potassium** are far apart in the activity series relative to magnesium and iron, making them incorrect options.
 
• The placement of metals like zinc in the activity series is based on their ability to displace hydrogen from acids and water. Zinc can displace hydrogen from acids, confirming its position above iron but below magnesium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Activity Series of Metals:**

 
 
• The activity series is a chart that ranks metals based on their reactivity. Metals at the top, like potassium and sodium, are highly reactive, while metals at the bottom, like gold and silver, are least reactive.
 
• Metals higher in the series can displace metals lower in the series from their compounds during reactions.
 
• For example, magnesium can displace zinc from zinc sulfate, while zinc can displace iron from iron sulfate.
 
 
 
• **Position of Zinc:**
 
 
• **Zinc** is positioned below magnesium but above iron in the activity series.
 
• It reacts with acids to produce hydrogen gas, confirming its reactivity, though it cannot displace magnesium or other more reactive metals.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Other Metals:**
 
 
• **Copper:** A less reactive metal that lies below zinc and iron in the activity series. It does not react with acids under normal conditions to displace hydrogen.
 
• **Silver:** A noble metal, highly resistant to corrosion and oxidation, placed even lower than copper in the activity series.
 
• **Potassium:** A highly reactive alkali metal placed at the top of the activity series, far above magnesium, zinc, and iron.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Zinc:**
 
 
• **Galvanization:** Zinc is used to coat iron or steel to prevent rusting.
 
• **Alloy Formation:** It is used in making alloys like brass (zinc and copper).
 
• **Batteries:** Zinc is used in dry cell batteries as an anode material.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reactivity Series Order:** Some key metals in decreasing order of reactivity are: Potassium > Sodium > Magnesium > Zinc > Iron > Copper > Silver > Gold.
 
• **Displacement Reactions:** Metals higher in the series displace metals lower in the series from solutions of their salts.
 
• **Practical Uses:** Understanding the activity series is critical in industrial processes such as extraction of metals, corrosion prevention, and galvanization.
